why: Which channel a guest's `dispatchAction` host effect re-enters, and with which invocation. An id the app DECLARES as a command re-enters the typed command channel addressed `{owner:{app:{pluginId,appId}},commandId}`; everything else — every framework-reserved verb (`toolRunStart`, `toolRunAbort`, `flowEvalTick`), every window action — re-enters the scoped ACTION channel addressed `{pluginId,appId,modeId,windowKindId,windowInstanceId,actionId}` with `windowId` folded into the arguments. Addressing a reserved verb as an app-owned command is REFUSED by the guest's own ownership gate (`dispatch_command`, `💻️os/🔨️modules/🔌️plugin/🦀️.rs` → `command '<id>' is not owned by app <app>`), and a refused re-arm is a dropped continuation. The wgpu bridge addressed every re-arm as an app command, so `toolRunStart` was refused at boot on 6118 (`[DEBUG] contributions rearm failed toolRunStart command 'toolRunStart' is not owned by app s.procedural.generation3d@1/*#editor`) and the preview evaluation's `ToolRunView` never reached the guest's surface: `cancellable:false` in all 206 status samples of a run where React — same guest, same instant — publishes `cancellable:true` with `cancelArgs:{runId:"1",generation:0}` (ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END, `📓️wgpu-regressions-sweep-2026-09-15.md`).

cases.why: A declared app command keeps the typed command channel it was declared on.
The framework-reserved tool-run verb the wgpu bridge was refusing: it belongs to the action channel, fully scoped, with `windowId` folded in.
An effect with no arguments still carries its own window id.
